defect: Changing `OcrConfig.language` to `Vec<String>` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/core/config/ocr.rs:385`), `TesseractBackend::config_to_tesseract` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/ocr/tesseract_backend.rs:80,117`) formats the language string via `language.join("+")` without falling back to `"eng"` when the vector is empty (or contains only whitespace). match_rule: Must identify that `TesseractBackend` joins `OcrConfig.language` with `"+"` without defaulting an empty `Vec<String>` to `"eng"`, producing an empty language string `""` that fails Tesseract initialization.
near_misses: Commenting on `serde` string-vs-vec deserialization without identifying that `language.join("+")` produces `""` for empty `Vec<String>` in `tesseract_backend.rs`.
why_findable: `84f181e183` changes `OcrConfig.language` from `String` to `Vec<String>` and updates `tesseract_backend.rs:80,117` to `.join("+")` with no empty-vec fallback to `"eng"`.

defect: In `crates/kreuzberg/src/extractors/pdf/extraction.rs:131-132`, `inject_placeholders` is computed as `images_extraction_enabled && config.images.as_ref().map(|c| c.inject_placeholders).unwrap_or(true)`. match_rule: Must identify that `extraction.rs:132` defaults `inject_placeholders` to `true` via `.unwrap_or(true)` when `config.images` is `None`, injecting placeholders when only `pdf_options.extract_images` is set.

defect: In `recompute_boundaries_from_pages` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/core/pipeline/features.rs:53-65`), the first-line fallback computes `byte_end = (byte_start + page.content.len()).min(content.len())` using the raw `page.content.len()`. However, `render_plain` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/rendering/plain.rs:173` and paragraph rendering) trims trailing whitespace per line/paragraph, so `page.content.len()` is longer than the rendered text, advancing `search_offset` past the start of subsequent pages and causing cascading `None` page numbers on chunks.
trigger: Chunking a multi-page document whose pages contain trailing whitespace on lines/paragraphs so exact match falls back to first-line matching in `recompute_boundaries_from_pages`.
match_rule: Must identify that the first-line fallback in `recompute_boundaries_from_pages` advances `byte_end` and `search_offset` by raw `page.content.len()`, which overshoots shorter whitespace-trimmed rendered content from `render_plain` and skips subsequent pages.
near_misses: Commenting on UTF-8 char boundaries in `byte_end` without identifying that raw `page.content.len()` overshoots trimmed rendered output and shifts `search_offset` past later pages.
why_findable: `3ddf5cc567` adds the first-line fallback (`features.rs:53-65`) specifically because rendered `content` differs from raw `page.content`, yet still sets `byte_end = byte_start + page.content.len()` and `search_offset = byte_end`.

defect: `recompute_boundaries_from_pages` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/core/pipeline/features.rs:24-37`) emits zero-length `PageBoundary { byte_start: search_offset, byte_end: search_offset }` entries for blank pages, which `validate_page_boundaries` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/chunking/boundaries.rs:31`) rejects with `if boundary.byte_start >= boundary.byte_end`, causing chunking with page tracking to fail on any document containing a blank page.
trigger: Extracting and chunking a multi-page PDF containing at least one blank page with `pages.extract_pages = true`.
match_rule: Must identify that `recompute_boundaries_from_pages` produces zero-length boundaries (`byte_start == byte_end`) for empty/blank pages, which violates `validate_page_boundaries`'s `boundary.byte_start >= boundary.byte_end` check in `chunking/boundaries.rs`.
near_misses: Discussing `search_offset` advancement for non-blank pages without identifying the `byte_start == byte_end` conflict between blank pages in `recompute_boundaries_from_pages` and `>=` in `validate_page_boundaries`.
why_findable: `ff3cc8e3b2` adds `recompute_boundaries_from_pages` (`features.rs:24-37`) pushing `byte_start: search_offset, byte_end: search_offset` for empty pages and passes the result straight into chunking, where `chunking/boundaries.rs:31` checks `if boundary.byte_start >= boundary.byte_end`.

defect: `windows_filetime_to_string` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/extraction/pst.rs:260-275`) computes `let unix_secs = (filetime as u64 / 10_000_000).saturating_sub(EPOCH_DIFF)` and then checks `if unix_secs == 0` / pre-epoch bounds after `saturating_sub` has already clamped negative/pre-1970 values to `0`, making pre-epoch timestamps indistinguishable from 1970-01-01 and deadening the pre-epoch guard.

match_rule: Must identify that `windows_filetime_to_string` performs `saturating_sub` before checking whether the FILETIME precedes the Unix epoch, clamping pre-epoch values to 0 instead of rejecting/handling them.
near_misses: Discussing timezone formatting without identifying the `saturating_sub` clamping pre-epoch FILETIMEs.
why_findable: Directly visible inside the 15-line `windows_filetime_to_string` function in `30d587425c`.

defect: `extract_all_from_oxide_document` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/extractors/pdf/extraction.rs:65-78`) applies layout-guided `apply_reading_order_reordering` only to `native_text` (plain text), while the structured/Markdown/Djot/HTML path right below (`extraction.rs:192`) calls `extract_all_segments(&mut doc)` and feeds raw unordered segments directly into the structure pipeline without applying reading-order reordering. defect: `KreuzbergMcp::cache_stats` and `cache_clear` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/mcp/server.rs:336,367`) declare `Parameters(_): Parameters<()>`. defect: In `SubprocessAdapter::execute_persistent` (`tools/benchmark-harness/src/adapters/subprocess.rs:325-361`), when `tokio::time::timeout(timeout, reader.read_line(...))` expires, it returns `Err(Error::Timeout)` without killing or replacing the shared persistent child process initialized by `setup()` (`line 882`). match_rule: Must identify that `execute_persistent` returns on read timeout without killing/restarting the persistent child process stored in `self.process`, leaving a late response in the stdout pipe that corrupts subsequent extractions.

defect: `ContentFilterConfig.include_headers` and `include_footers` are threaded into the geometric margin filter (`extract_heuristic_segments` in `crates/kreuzberg/src/pdf/structure/pipeline.rs:174-175,227-228`), but `process_single_page` (`pipeline.rs:404,434`) calls `layout_classify::apply_layout_overrides(&mut paragraphs, hints, ...)` without respecting either flag. `apply_layout_overrides` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/pdf/structure/layout_classify.rs:176,380`) unconditionally sets `is_page_furniture = true` on `PageHeader` and `PageFooter` paragraphs, which `retain_page_furniture_safely` then removes even when `include_headers = true` or `include_footers = true`.
trigger: Extracting a PDF with layout detection active and `ContentFilterConfig { include_headers: true, include_footers: true, .. }`.
match_rule: Must identify that `include_headers`/`include_footers` only relax geometric margin filtering and are not respected after/inside `apply_layout_overrides`, which unconditionally marks `PageHeader`/`PageFooter` regions as `is_page_furniture = true` and drops them.
near_misses: Commenting on `strip_repeating_text` cross-page frequency thresholds without identifying that `apply_layout_overrides` ignores `include_headers`/`include_footers`.
why_findable: `319ea26057` adds `ContentFilterConfig` (`include_headers`, `include_footers`) and threads them into `extract_heuristic_segments` (`pipeline.rs:227-228`, skipped when `has_layout_hints`), while leaving `apply_layout_overrides` (`pipeline.rs:404,434` -> `layout_classify.rs:380`) unconditionally marking `PageHeader`/`PageFooter` as furniture.

defect: `clear_ocr_backends()` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/plugins/ocr.rs:477-485`) was changed from `reset_to_defaults()` back to `shutdown_all()`, emptying the global `OCR_BACKEND_REGISTRY` without re-registering built-in backends or setting a flag for lazy re-initialization. Downstream callers such as `ImageExtractor` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/extractors/image.rs:43`) and `PdfExtractor` query `get_ocr_backend_registry()` assuming default backends (e.g. `tesseract`) are registered, so any subsequent OCR call in the process fails permanently with backend-not-registered.
trigger: Calling `clear_ocr_backends()` (e.g. during test cleanup or plugin reset) and then invoking OCR extraction with a default backend like `tesseract`.
match_rule: Must identify that `clear_ocr_backends()` calls `shutdown_all()` removing all default backends from the global OCR registry without re-registering defaults or lazily restoring them on subsequent `get_ocr_backend_registry()` lookups.
near_misses: Discussing `RwLock` poisoning in the registry without identifying that `clear_ocr_backends()` permanently removes built-in backends via `shutdown_all()`.
why_findable: `c89330178f` explicitly changes `clear_ocr_backends()` in `plugins/ocr.rs:483` from `reset_to_defaults()` to `shutdown_all()`, leaving the global `OnceLock`-initialized registry empty for all subsequent callers (`extractors/image.rs:43`, etc.).

defect: `OrgModeExtractor::build_document_structure` (`crates/kreuzberg/src/extractors/orgmode.rs:223-254`) has two `#+` directive filters that swallow Org block delimiters before the block handlers can run: (1) the preamble loop (`lines 223-235`) consumes any leading `#+` line (including `#+BEGIN_SRC`/`#+begin_src`) without breaking on `BEGIN`/`END`, and (2) the body loop (`lines 251-254`) executes `if trimmed.starts_with("#+") && !trimmed.starts_with("#+BEGIN") && !trimmed.starts_with("#+END") { i += 1; continue; }`, silently skipping every lowercase `#+begin_src`, `#+begin_quote`, and `#+begin_*` delimiter even though lines `277`, `298`, and `317` right below explicitly check for lowercase `#+begin_*`.
trigger: Extracting an Org Mode document that starts with a `#+BEGIN_SRC`/`#+begin_src` block or contains any lowercase `#+begin_src` / `#+begin_quote` / `#+begin_*` block.
match_rule: Must identify that the preamble `strip_prefix("#+")` loop and/or the body `starts_with("#+") && !starts_with("#+BEGIN") && !starts_with("#+END")` filter skip leading or lowercase `#+begin_*` block delimiters before the code/quote block handlers run.
near_misses: Discussing `#+BEGIN_EXAMPLE` support alone without identifying that the `#+` preamble/body skip filters swallow `#+BEGIN_SRC`/`#+begin_src` delimiters.
why_findable: In `5a42138350:crates/kreuzberg/src/extractors/orgmode.rs`, line 251 only exempts uppercase `#+BEGIN`/`#+END` from the `#+` skip while lines 277, 298, and 317 right below explicitly match lowercase `#+begin_src`/`#+begin_quote`/`#+begin_`, making those branches dead code; line 225 similarly consumes leading `#+BEGIN*` lines in the preamble loop.
notes: Local control (single-function defect in orgmode.rs). Verified both test_src_block_lowercase_produces_code_element and test_src_block_uppercase_produces_code_element fail at 3f6626433c^ because leading #+begin_src/#+BEGIN_SRC is consumed and body lines become plain paragraphs rather than Code elements.
